sql:
SELECT COUNT(1) AS n
FROM   TPCDS_DB.store_sales ss
LEFT JOIN TPCDS_DB.promotion p ON ss.ss_promo_sk = p.p_promo_sk
WHERE  ss.ss_customer_sk IS NULL

attempts.sql: SELECT COUNT(1) AS n FROM TPCDS_DB.store_sales ss WHERE ss.ss_customer_sk IS NULL
attempts.change_summary: Removed the unnecessary LEFT JOIN to promotion table since its columns are not referenced in the SELECT and the join cannot affect the row count when counting rows from the left table with a LEFT JOIN.

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query executes an unnecessary LEFT JOIN to the promotion table (300 rows) when only counting store_sales rows where ss_customer_sk IS NULL; the join adds broadcast and hash-join overhead without affecting the count.

plan_nodes.note: LeftOuter BuildRight; Left keys [1]: [ss_promo_sk#57851]; Right keys [1]: [p_promo_sk#57866]; Join type: LeftOuter; Join

hypotheses.claim: A LEFT JOIN whose columns are never read still costs a join; if the joined key is unique it cannot change the rows and can be removed. (matched: left join tpcds_db.promotion p on ss.ss_promo_sk = p.p_promo_sk)

The LEFT JOIN is semantically redundant for COUNT(*) because no columns from promotion are selected and a LEFT JOIN cannot reduce the left-side row count; removing the join would eliminate the broadcast and join entirely.
Broadcasting the 300-row promotion table is wasted work if the join is removed; the broadcast exchange and build-side preparation would disappear.
The scan of store_sales with pushed IsNull(ss_customer_sk) filter is the remaining dominant cost; its runtime depends on the selectivity of ss_customer_sk IS NULL and the table size.
